chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah said:

I asked him about a woman who dies before the husband enters into her, or the husband dies before he enters into her. He said: Whichever of them dies, the woman receives half of what was stipulated for her. And if no dowry was stipulated for her, then she has no dowry.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dowry if the husband or wife dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the financial rights in the event of death prior to consummation, establishing that half the stipulated dowry is due to the survivor, while no dowry is owed if none was specified. This ruling is derived from the general principle in Surah An-Nisa that the dowry is a gift, with the half-share reflecting the partial completion of the marriage contract's primary purpose. It highlights the Shia juristic view on the proportionality of financial obligations relative to the status of the marital bond.
